body.p: Claims 1-30 have been previously cancelled. Claims 42, 48, and 49 have been

amended. No new matter has been added. Thus, claims 31-51 are pending in the present application. In view of the above amendments and the following remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that all of the currently pending claims are in condition for allowance.
Claims 31-41 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as directed to an abstract idea without significantly more.

Claim 31 recites a method for non-invasive determination of a hemodynamic parameter of a subject mechanically ventilated via a breathing apparatus based on a point in time, thb, of a heartbeat of the subject and an arrival point in time, tarr_pulm, at which a blood pressure pulse caused by the heartbeat reaches lungs of the subject, comprising "determining the point in time, thb, of the heartbeat of the subject based on data measured via a blood oxygen sensor" and "measuring a respiratory pressure and/or a respiratory flow via one of a pressure sensor and a flow sensor of the breathing apparatus" along with "determining, via a controller of the breathing apparatus, tarr_pulm from a change in the measured respiratory pressure and/or the respiratory flow resulting from a change in lung volume caused by the arrival of the blood pressure pulse to the lungs" and "determining, via the controller, a pulmonary pulse transit time, PTTpulm, for the blood pressure pulse based on thb and tarr_pulm" and "determining, via the controller, the hemodynamic parameter based on PTTpulm."
It is respectfully submitted that amended claim 31 satisfies the requirements of

patentability and is thus allowable over 35 U.S.C. § 101. According to MPEP 2106, the claimed invention must qualify as patent-eligible subject matter - i.e., the claim must not be directed to a judicial exception (step 2A) unless the claim as a whole includes additional imitations amounting to significantly more than the exception (step 2B). Step 2A is a two-prong analysis: 1) whether the claim recites an abstract idea, law of nature, or a natural phenomenon, and 2) whether the claim recites additional elements that integrate the judicial exception into a practical application.

With respect to the first prong of the Step 2A analysis, the Examiner contends that the claim recites an abstract idea and, in particular, mathematical relationships/calculations and/or mental process. Applicant respectfully maintains that a claim does not recite a mathematical

concept if it is only based on or involves a mathematical concept. MPEP 2106.04(a)(2) states that "a limitation that is merely based on or involves a mathematical concept described in the specification may not be sufficient to fall into this grouping, provided that the mathematical concept itself is not recited in the claim." Indeed, the pulmonary pulse transit time is recited as being based on the point in time of the heartbeat and the arrival point in time of the arrival blood pressure pulse to the lungs and the hemodynamic parameter is recited as being based on the pulmonary transit time. Additionally, with respect to Examiner's claim that such language may, alternatively, be indicative of a mental process, Applicant respectfully disagrees. It is

respectfully submitted that the claim limitations cannot practically be performed via the human mind. In particular, the limitation of "determining the point in time, thb, of the heartbeat of thesubject based on data measured via a blood oxygen sensor" requires more than mereobservation and/or generic evaluation of the blood oxygen sensor data to determine the point intime, thb, of the heartbeat of the subject based thereon. While the Examiner notes that a bloodoxygen sensor such as, for example, a pulse oximeter, is capable of measuring pulse data, it is

respectfully submitted that the pulse data provided by such a sensor is a heart rate of the subject and that a point in time of a heartbeat is not identifiable from observation or genericevaluation of such data. Thus, it is respectfully submitted that the claim limitations do not recitean abstract idea.
Even if, however, the claim could be determined as reciting an abstract idea, it is

respectfully submitted that the purported abstract idea is integrated into a practical application and is thus not directed to a judicial exception under prong 2 of the Step 2A analysis. Inparticular, it is submitted that the purported abstract idea is implemented with or used inconjunction with a particular machine or manufacture that is integral to the recited claim. SeeMPEP 2106.05(b). The blood oxygen sensor, in particular, is not being utilized in a genericfashion according to a conventional breathing apparatus. As noted above, a blood oxygensensor such as, for example, a pulse oximeter, is capable of providing pulse data in addition toblood oxygenation data. It is submitted that the pulse data, however, is not indicative of a pointin time of a heartbeat of the subject. Rather, as would be understood by those of skill in the art,a pulse oximeter detects changes in light absorption caused by pulsating blood through thearteries, so that a heart rate may be calculated. Thus, a conventional blood oxygen sensor,when used in conjunction with a breathing apparatus, merely monitors a subject's blood oxygenconcentration and/or heart rate during ventilation. According to the recited claim, however, theblood oxygen sensor, and its corresponding data, is utilized to determine a point in time of a

heartbeat of the subject. It is respectfully submitted that the blood oxygen sensor according to the recited claim clearly does not conform to a generic and/or conventional usage thereof such that the purported abstract idea is integrated into a practical application.

Furthermore, at the very least, under Step 2B, it is respectfully submitted that the claim includes additional elements amounting to significantly more than the purported judicial exception. The Examiner contends that obtaining pulse data via a blood oxygen sensor Is considered a data gathering step of insignificant extra-solution activity (MPEP 2106.05(g)) and mere instructions to implement an abstract idea on a computer (MPEP 2106.05(f)). Applicant respectfully disagrees. The limitations of the claim are applied via a particular machine and provide clear improvement/change in the function of the machine (e.g., breathing apparatus). As noted above, a generic/conventional usage of a blood oxygen sensor and a breathing apparatus does not determine a point in time of a heartbeat, as required by the recited claim. As would be understood by those of skill in the art and as noted in the Specification, usage of a blood oxygen sensor to determine a point in time of a heartbeat is a clear improvement over existing systems, which rely on additional peripheral equipment such as, for example, ECG sensors. See Specification, p. 3, ll. 1-7. As further evidenced via the lack of prior art, non- invasive determinations of arrival point in time of blood pressure pulses based to the lung based on respiratory pressure/flow, and pulse transit times determined therefrom, as recited in the claim, is a new, inventive concept. The Specification clearly differentiates between pulmonary flow induced measurements, as recited in the claim, and traditionally obtained systemic measurements. Thus, it is submitted that the claim provides more than mere data collection and includes an inventive concept - i.e., significantly more.

Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that claim 31 is allowable over 35 U.S.C. § 101 and that the rejection of this claim should be withdrawn. Because claims 32-40 depend from and include all of the limitations of claim 31, it is respectfully submitted that these claims are also allowable.

Claim 41 recites limitations substantially similar to the limitations of claim 31. Thus, for at least the same reasons as discussed above with respect to claim 31, it is respectfully submitted that claim 41 is also allowable over 35 U.S.C. § 101.

It is respectfully noted that claim 42 has been amended to recite limitations substantially similar to claim 31. Thus, it is respectfully submitted that claim 42 and its dependent claims are also allowable over 35 U.S.C. § 101.

In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully submitted that all of the currently pending claims are in condition for allowance. All issues raised by the Examiner having been addressed, an early and favorable action on the merits is earnestly solicited.
Respectfully submitted,
